hints: Focus on what complete combustion of an alcohol actually makes, and then ask yourself which of those products is really a gas at s.t.p.
Work out the moles of pentan-1-ol first, its Mr is 88, so 17.6 g is 0.20 mol, and each mole gives 5 moles of CO2.
Convert only the moles of gas that stays gaseous at 0 C to volume using 22.4 dm3 per mole, remembering water condenses to liquid.
walkthrough:
**Find moles of pentan-1-ol**

Pentan-1-ol is $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{11}\text{OH}$, which is $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$. Its Mr is 88.0.

$$n = \frac{m}{M_r} = \frac{17.6}{88.0} = 0.20 \text{ mol}$$

**Write the complete combustion equation**

Complete combustion of a fuel containing C, H and O gives carbon dioxide and water.

$$\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O} + 7.5\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 5\text{CO}_2 + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Decide what is gaseous at s.t.p.**

This is the key trick. s.t.p. is $0^{\circ}\text{C}$ and 1 atm. At that low temperature, water is liquid, not steam. So the only gaseous product is $\text{CO}_2$.

**Calculate volume of CO2**

Moles of $\text{CO}_2 = 0.20 \times 5 = 1.0 \text{ mol}$.

At s.t.p., 1 mol of gas occupies $22.4 \text{ dm}^3$.

$$V = 1.0 \times 22.4 = 22.4 \text{ dm}^3$$

options.A: Correct. 0.20 mol of alcohol produces 1.0 mol of CO2. Only CO2 is gaseous at s.t.p. because water is liquid, so volume is 1.0 x 22.4 = 22.4 dm3.
options.B: Incorrect. This uses 24.0 dm3 per mole, which is the molar volume at room temperature and pressure, not s.t.p. It also correctly counts only CO2, but with the wrong molar volume.
options.C: Incorrect. This counts both CO2 and H2O as gases: 0.20 x 11 = 2.2 mol x 22.4 = 49.3 dm3. The trap is forgetting that water condenses to a liquid at s.t.p. (0 C).
options.D: Incorrect. This makes two errors at once, counting water as a gas and using room conditions: 2.2 mol x 24.0 = 52.8 dm3. It combines both common traps.
